html:
New Netherland was the Dutch colony on the Hudson, Delaware and Connecticut rivers in North America, from 1614 until 1664, when the English took it and renamed it New York. Its capital was New Amsterdam on Manhattan.

Henry Hudson sailed up the river for the Dutch East India Company in 1609, and traders followed. From 1621 the Dutch West India Company ran the colony as a business, above all for the beaver fur trade. At Fort Orange, now Albany, the Dutch bought pelts from the Mahican and the Mohawk, and Dutch guns helped the Haudenosaunee in their wars with their neighbours.

Relations with the Munsee Lenape around Manhattan and the Wappinger up the river turned to war in the 1640s, when the director Willem Kieft attacked their villages. Peter Stuyvesant, director from 1647, took over New Sweden on the Delaware in 1655. The colony was small but mixed: Dutch, Walloons, Germans, enslaved and free Africans, and Jews from Brazil.

In 1664 an English fleet arrived and Stuyvesant gave up without a fight. The Dutch retook it briefly in 1673 and then gave it up for good by treaty in 1674.
sum: New Netherland was the Dutch colony on the Hudson, Delaware and Connecticut rivers in North America, from 1614 until 1664, when the English took it and renamed it New York. Its capital was New Amsterdam on Manhattan.
